name: ebitda_l3_growth_return_leverage
mechanism: In a Gordon-style valuation, EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and with how efficiently growth is funded (ROIC), and falls with financial risk. Industry peers share the same business risk and accounting conventions, so ranking within the industry on growth, ROIC and net leverage should isolate peers with the same fundamental multiple drivers, closer than the industry as a whole.
prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of the 4 exploration years, with the pooled median at or below 0.32.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Growth, ROIC and risk are the standard drivers of EV/EBITDA, and the recipe ranks on them inside an L3 screen with a sensible fallback, so the prediction is testable; note that EV multiples are only weakly sensitive to leverage and log_sales is not part of the stated mechanism, so keep those weights low.

name: sales_l2_margin_matched
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so most of the spread in sales multiples comes from differences in profitability. Within a broad 2-digit industry, picking peers with the closest EBITDA and gross margins (plus growth) cancels out the margin term that a plain industry median ignores.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at least 0.08 below the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline (0.603), i.e. at or below 0.52, and better in all 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: The identity EV/Sales = EV/EBITDA x EBITDA margin is a clear reason to match on margins, the ranking does exactly that, and the year-by-year and pooled targets are falsifiable.

name: sales_crossindustry_profitability_twins
mechanism: Once margins, growth and capital intensity are matched, firms produce similar free cash flow per dollar of sales, whatever their SIC code. Searching the whole cross-section for profitability twins gives a larger and closer-matched peer set than industry codes, which often group businesses with very different economics.
prediction: Beats the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline in at least 3 of 4 years, with a pooled median at or below 0.55.
compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 0.5, asset_turnover 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=5
critic_reason: Matching on cash conversion per dollar of sales across the whole cross-section is a new idea, distinct from industry screens, the rank features implement it, and the prediction can be tested against the L3 baseline.

name: ebitda_l2_size_band_reinvestment
mechanism: EBITDA overstates distributable cash flow for capital-heavy firms, because capex absorbs part of it. So at equal growth, firms with higher capex intensity should trade at lower EBITDA multiples. Size, in turn, proxies for risk and liquidity premia. Matching on reinvestment needs, growth and margin within a 2-digit industry and a size band should capture both effects.
prediction: Median |ln error| at or below 0.33, beating the warranted-multiple regression (0.357) in all 4 years and the L3 industry median in at least 2 of 4.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band log_sales±1.5 | rank capex_intensity 1, sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Capex intensity explains why EBITDA overstates distributable cash, and the size band covers risk premia, both implemented through the screens and ranking with falsifiable targets; the ebitda_margin rank term is only loosely motivated, so justify it or drop it.

name: ebitda_l4_cascade_growth_roic
mechanism: Narrow 4-digit SIC peers share product markets, customers and cyclicality, so they face the same discount rate and the same long-run growth outlook. Within that narrow group, a small ranking on growth and ROIC refines the match, and the cascade to L3 and L2 keeps coverage when narrow industries are thin.
prediction: Beats the L3 industry median (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 years, and the gain is concentrated among firms that end up with L4 peers.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: Narrow SIC peers sharing product markets and cyclicality is a sensible mechanism, the L4->L3->L2 cascade implements it, and the claim that gains concentrate among firms with L4 peers is a specific, testable prediction.

name: sales_l3_margin_band_growth_size
mechanism: A hard band on EBITDA margin makes sure every peer converts sales into cash flow at a similar rate, which is the main driver of EV/Sales. Within that band and the 3-digit industry, ranking on growth and size captures the remaining differences in duration and risk. The fallbacks relax the industry screen before they relax the margin match.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at or below 0.53, beating the L3 industry-median EV/Sales baseline in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.04]
critic_reason: A hard EBITDA-margin band targets the main driver of EV/Sales directly, and the fallbacks relax the industry screen before the margin match, as the mechanism says; watch coverage, since a +/-0.05 band inside L3 with min_peers=4 may push many targets onto the cross-industry fallback.

name: harmonic_l3_reinvestment_adjusted_ebitda
mechanism: Multiples are ratios of value to earnings, so averaging them arithmetically overweights the high-multiple peers. The harmonic mean is equivalent to pooling peer values over pooled earnings, which is less biased upward. Within 3-digit industry peers, ranking on growth, ROIC and reinvestment needs (capex intensity) matches the three drivers of the value-to-EBITDA ratio in a steady-state model: g, the return on reinvested capital, and the part of EBITDA that is not free cash flow.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.325 and beats the L3/L2 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a mean error below the industry baseline's 0.513.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 0.75, log_assets 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Adds capex intensity as an explicit reinvestment driver from the steady-state EV/EBITDA identity (g, return on reinvested capital, non-FCF share of EBITDA) and drops leverage, so it is a real change from g01-01 rather than a k/aggregator tweak, and the prediction is falsifiable; note that the harmonic mean equals pooled value over pooled earnings only under equal value weights, so treat that claim as approximate.

name: da_burden_twins_ebitda
mechanism: EBITDA leaves out depreciation and amortization, but D&A stands for real asset-replacement costs. The gap between EBITDA margin and EBIT margin measures how much of EBITDA goes to maintaining the asset base, so firms with the same EBITDA but heavier D&A should trade at lower EBITDA multiples. Matching on both margins at once (plus growth and balance-sheet leverage), within a 2-digit industry and a size band, picks peers whose EBITDA converts into operating profit at the same rate.
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a median error at or below 0.330.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band log_sales±2 | rank ebit_margin 1, ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, debt_to_assets 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: The D&A-burden idea (EBITDA-to-EBIT conversion as a proxy for maintenance capex) is a new and economically grounded mechanism, matching both margins together does pin down their gap, and the screens and prediction are specific and falsifiable.

name: leverage_banded_industry_ebitda
mechanism: Enterprise-value multiples of heavily indebted firms show distress costs, tax shields and covenant constraints that unlevered peers do not share. A hard band on net debt/EBITDA keeps every peer in the same capital-structure regime before the ranking. Within that band and the 3-digit industry, ranking on margin, growth and asset turnover matches profitability and capital efficiency, and a trimmed mean limits the influence of any one outlier peer.
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with the largest gain among firms in the top tercile of net debt/EBITDA.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3, band net_debt_to_ebitda±2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, asset_turnover 0.5 | k=8, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2, band net_debt_to_ebitda±2] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: A hard net-debt/EBITDA band is a new screen with a clear capital-structure rationale (EV/EBITDA mechanically includes net debt/EBITDA, plus distress and tax-shield effects), the recipe implements it directly, and the tercile-specific prediction is sharply falsifiable.

name: margin_growth_box_sales
mechanism: EV/Sales is roughly cash margin times a duration factor that depends on growth. Hard bands on EBITDA margin and on sales growth together pin down both parts directly, whatever the SIC code. Inside that box, ranking on size, capital intensity and gross margin covers the remaining risk and reinvestment differences. The fallbacks drop the growth constraint first and then widen the margin band.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.40 and beats the L3/L2 industry median in all 4 years, with coverage of at least 95%.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03, band sales_growth_1y±0.1 | rank log_sales 1, capex_intensity 1, gross_margin 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08]
critic_reason: Boxing on margin and growth together follows the EV/Sales = margin x duration decomposition and the growth band is new compared with g01-03/g01-06, but the first fallback drops growth and also widens the margin band to 0.05 rather than doing one step at a time, so describe that accurately, and be aware that ignoring industry assumes discount rates are similar across sectors.

name: harmonic_l2_margin_band_roic_sales
mechanism: Once a margin band fixes how much cash each dollar of sales produces, the rest of the EV/Sales spread comes from how much capital that growth needs, measured by ROIC and asset turnover. Within a 2-digit industry and an EBITDA-margin band, ranking on growth, ROIC and turnover matches value creation per dollar of sales. The harmonic mean then guards against the right-skew that sales multiples typically have.
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a mean error below 0.60.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.04 | rank roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, asset_turnover 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08]
critic_reason: Adding ROIC and asset turnover inside a margin band brings in a new capital-efficiency idea compared with g01-06, and the prediction is falsifiable; note that with margin held fixed, ROIC and turnover largely overlap, so the ranking effectively double-weights capital intensity.

name: l4_cascade_profitability_twins_sales
mechanism: 4-digit SIC peers share product markets, pricing power and cyclicality, so their discount rates and long-run growth are similar. Inside that narrow group, ranking mainly on EBITDA and EBIT margins removes the profitability term that drives EV/Sales. The cascade widens the industry only as far as coverage needs, so the narrow industry match is kept whenever it is available.
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median in all 4 years, with a median error at or below 0.45.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l4 | rank ebitda_margin 2, ebit_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=6, trimmed_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Applying the L4->L3->L2 cascade to EV/Sales with margin-twin ranking is a new screen for this multiple and the mechanism is coherent and falsifiable, though it is close to recombining g01-05's screen with g01-02's ranking, and ebit_margin is highly correlated with ebitda_margin, so it adds little separate information.

name: ebitda_l3_size_band_growth_roic
mechanism: Discount rates differ systematically with firm size: small firms carry liquidity and risk premia, so they trade at lower EBITDA multiples than large firms in the same industry with the same growth. A hard size band inside the 3-digit industry fixes this risk-premium dimension before ranking on growth, ROIC and reinvestment needs, which are the remaining Gordon-model drivers of value per unit of EBITDA.
prediction: Median error below the L3/L2 industry median (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with coverage of at least 98%.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3, band log_sales±1.5 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2, band log_sales±1.5] -> [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: This recombines components already tried without a new economic idea: the size-band-inside-industry discount-rate mechanism was tested in g01-04 (L2 + log_sales±1.5), and the L3 growth/ROIC/capex ranking with a size term is g02-01, so swapping L2 for L3 and a soft size rank for the same hard band is a trivial variant.
reason: critic: This recombines components already tried without a new economic idea: the size-band-inside-industry discount-rate mechanism was tested in g01-04 (L2 + log_sales±1.5), and the L3 growth/ROIC/capex ranking with a size term is g02-01, so swapping L2 for L3 and a soft size rank for the same hard band is a trivial variant.

name: ebitda_l2_growth_regime_band
mechanism: Expected growth is the single largest driver of an EBITDA multiple, and fast and slow growers in one industry are priced as different assets. A hard band on 1-year sales growth inside the 2-digit industry puts every peer in the same growth regime, and ranking on ROIC, capex intensity, net leverage and asset size then matches how cheaply that growth is funded and how risky the claim is.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with median error at or below 0.330.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band sales_growth_1y±0.1 | rank roic 1, capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_assets 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2, band sales_growth_1y±0.2] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: A hard growth-regime band inside the industry is a new screen for EV/EBITDA (growth has only been ranked, never boxed, within industry), the mechanism that growth is the main multiple driver is sensible, the ROIC/capex/leverage/size ranks match the stated funding-cost and risk story, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_crosssection_conversion_twins
mechanism: An EBITDA multiple equals value over a pre-reinvestment cash flow, so it depends on growth, on the return earned on reinvestment, on the share of EBITDA lost to D&A and capex, and on financial risk, none of which require a shared SIC code. Boxing candidates on growth and net leverage across the whole cross-section and ranking on ROIC, both margins (whose gap is the D&A burden), capex intensity and size finds fundamental twins that industry codes can miss.
prediction: Median error below 0.345 with coverage above 95%; if it does not beat the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years, industry membership carries EV/EBITDA information beyond these fundamentals.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen band sales_growth_1y±0.1, band net_debt_to_ebitda±1.5 | rank roic 1, ebit_margin 1, ebitda_margin 1, capex_intensity 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=8 | fallback [band sales_growth_1y±0.2] -> []
critic_reason: No industry-free EV/EBITDA recipe has been tried, the growth/leverage boxes and the ROIC, margin-gap, capex and size ranks implement the stated value-driver decomposition, and the prediction includes an explicit falsification condition about whether industry membership carries extra information.

name: sales_free_cash_margin_box
mechanism: EV/Sales scales with the free cash flow each dollar of sales produces, and pre-tax free cash margin is roughly EBITDA margin minus capex intensity. Hard bands on both put every peer at the same cash conversion whatever its SIC code, and ranking on growth, ROIC and size then matches duration, value creation on reinvestment and the risk premium.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.390 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years, with coverage of at least 90%.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04, band capex_intensity±0.04 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08]
critic_reason: Adding a hard capex-intensity band beside the EBITDA-margin band is a new screen that implements a clear free-cash-margin mechanism for EV/Sales, the growth/ROIC/size ranks match the duration, value-creation and risk story, and the 4-of-4-years prediction is falsifiable.

name: sales_l2_ebit_margin_band
mechanism: EBIT margin is profit after the cost of replacing the asset base (D&A), so it is a better proxy than EBITDA margin for the sustainable operating cash a dollar of sales produces. A hard EBIT-margin band inside the 2-digit industry fixes that term, and ranking on EBITDA margin (which, given EBIT margin, measures D&A intensity), growth and size matches the remaining differences in asset intensity, duration and risk.
prediction: Beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years, with median error below 0.410.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebit_margin±0.03 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebit_margin±0.03] -> [band ebit_margin±0.06]
critic_reason: Screening on EBIT margin rather than EBITDA margin is a new feature in a hard band, motivated by the sensible idea that post-D&A margin better measures sustainable cash per dollar of sales, the EBITDA-margin rank given an EBIT band does capture D&A intensity as claimed, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: sales_size_matched_margin_twins
mechanism: With the cash margin held fixed, sales multiples still differ by the discount rate, which falls with firm size (liquidity, diversification, access to capital) and rises with balance-sheet distress risk. Hard bands on EBITDA margin and on log sales put peers at the same profitability and risk-premium level, and ranking on growth, gross margin and debt-to-assets matches duration, pricing power and leverage risk.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.395 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years, with coverage of at least 90%.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03, band log_sales±1.5 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, debt_to_assets 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.03] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.06]
critic_reason: A hard size band has never been applied to EV/Sales, and pairing it with an EBITDA-margin box plus a new debt_to_assets rank implements the stated idea that discount rates vary with size and distress risk once margin is fixed, which differs from g02-04's growth box; the prediction is falsifiable.

name: sales_rnd_adjusted_margin_box
mechanism: R&D is expensed, so two firms with the same reported EBITDA margin can have very different economic cash margins: the R&D-heavy firm is investing part of its margin in intangible capital that markets capitalize into value, which raises its EV/Sales. A hard band on R&D intensity next to the EBITDA-margin band puts peers at the same reported margin AND the same hidden investment rate, and ranking on growth, gross margin and size then matches duration, pricing power and the risk premium. Fallbacks drop the R&D constraint (for firms with no reported R&D) before widening the margin band.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales in all 4 years with median error at or below 0.40, and does at least as well as g03-06 on R&D-intensive firms (rnd_intensity above 0.05).
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03, band rnd_intensity±0.03 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.03] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.06]
critic_reason: R&D intensity has never been used, and a hard band on it next to the EBITDA-margin band directly matches peers on how much investment is hidden by expensing, a sensible reason for EV/Sales to differ at equal reported margin; the fallbacks are well ordered and the R&D-subsample comparison with g03-06 is falsifiable.

name: sales_dupont_roa_box
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/Assets divided by asset turnover, and EBITDA margin times asset turnover is the pre-tax cash return on assets. Hard bands on both margin and turnover fix how much cash each dollar of sales produces and how much capital stands behind each dollar of sales, so peers share the same return on the asset base whatever their SIC code. Ranking on growth, ROIC and debt-to-assets then matches duration, value creation on new capital and financial risk.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales in all 4 years with median error at or below 0.40; coverage at least 90%.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03, band asset_turnover±0.25 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, debt_to_assets 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.03] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.06]
critic_reason: Hard-banding asset turnover together with EBITDA margin across industries carries out the DuPont identity (EV/Sales = EV/Assets / turnover, margin x turnover = cash ROA), a new cross-industry idea; turnover was only a low-weight rank feature inside an SIC screen before, and the error and coverage targets are falsifiable.

name: sales_operating_leverage_box
mechanism: Two firms with the same EBITDA margin but different gross margins have different cost structures: a high-gross-margin firm spends heavily on discretionary SG&A (marketing, customer acquisition) that is partly investment and gives strong operating leverage, so investors expect margin expansion and pay more per dollar of sales. Hard bands on both gross margin and EBITDA margin fix the current cash margin and the cost structure behind it, and ranking on growth, size and capex intensity matches duration, risk premium and reinvestment needs.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales in all 4 years and has median error at or below 0.40, with lower mean error than g01-03 (0.672).
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03, band gross_margin±0.06 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.03, band gross_margin±0.12] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.05]
critic_reason: This uses exactly the five features of g02-04 (EBITDA-margin band, growth, size, capex, gross margin) with screen and rank swapped, and g03-06 already ranked on gross margin at full weight inside an EBITDA-margin band, which is the same gross-versus-EBITDA cost-structure match, so the hard gross-margin band adds no new economic test; a new idea would need a feature that measures operating leverage directly.

name: ebitda_rnd_expensing_regime
mechanism: Because R&D is expensed, R&D-intensive firms report EBITDA that understates their pre-investment cash flow and carry growth options that the current EBITDA does not reflect, so they trade at systematically higher EV/EBITDA than low-R&D firms in the same broad industry. A hard band on R&D intensity inside the 2-digit industry keeps peers in the same expensing and growth-option regime, and ranking on growth, ROIC and net leverage matches the standard Gordon-model drivers; firms without R&D data fall back to plain industry peers.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band rnd_intensity±0.03 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: Banding on R&D intensity inside the 2-digit industry is a new screen with a clear reason (expensed R&D lowers EBITDA and signals growth options, raising EV/EBITDA), the recipe matches the mechanism with sensible fallbacks for firms without R&D, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_margin_cycle_position
mechanism: EBITDA margins mean-revert, so a firm whose margin is depressed relative to industry norms trades at a high EV/EBITDA (the market prices in a recovery), while a firm at peak margins trades at a low one. A hard band on EBITDA margin inside the 3-digit industry puts peers at the same point in the margin cycle, so they share the same expected recovery or fade; ranking on growth, ROIC and net leverage then matches the remaining value drivers.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.330, beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, and lower mean error than the industry median baseline (0.513).
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: Margin-cycle position means a firm's margin compared with its own normal level, but a band on the raw EBITDA margin level cannot tell a structurally low-margin firm from one at a cyclical trough (and those trade at opposite multiples), so the recipe does not carry out the mean-reversion mechanism; it would need a measure of margin deviation from the firm's or industry's history.

name: ebitda_pricing_power_moat
mechanism: Gross margin measures pricing power and product differentiation, which sets how long a firm can earn above its cost of capital (the competitive-advantage period). At equal near-term growth, a longer advantage period means a higher EV/EBITDA, and a broad 2-digit industry mixes branded and commodity producers. A gross-margin band inside the 2-digit industry keeps peers in the same competitive position, and ranking on growth, ROIC, net leverage and size matches the remaining drivers.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.330 and beats the industry median in all 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band gross_margin±0.08 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2, band gross_margin±0.15] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: A gross-margin band inside the 2-digit industry is a new screen for EV/EBITDA, linked by a clear argument (pricing power gives a longer competitive-advantage period and so a higher multiple at equal growth) to separating branded from commodity producers; the widening fallback is sensible and the all-4-years target is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_tax_burden_l3
mechanism: EV is a claim on unlevered after-tax cash flow, so at equal EBITDA, growth and reinvestment a firm that pays a higher effective tax rate keeps less of each EBITDA dollar and should trade at a lower EV/EBITDA. Given EBIT margin and balance-sheet leverage (which pins down interest), the remaining gap between EBIT margin and net margin mostly reflects the tax burden and recurring non-operating items, so ranking 3-digit industry peers jointly on growth, EBIT margin, net margin and debt-to-assets matches peers that convert EBITDA into after-tax unlevered cash at the same rate.

name: ebitda_asset_turnover_business_model
mechanism: Asset turnover is a stock measure of the business model (asset-light distributors and services versus asset-heavy manufacturers and utilities can share a 2-digit SIC code), and it determines how much capital must be added per dollar of future sales, i.e. how much of EBITDA growth is eaten by reinvestment. Unlike annual capex intensity, which is lumpy, turnover is stable year to year, so a hard turnover band inside the 2-digit industry keeps peers with the same capital needs per unit of growth, and ranking on growth, ROIC and net leverage matches the remaining Gordon-model drivers.

name: ebitda_expensed_investment_gap
mechanism: The gap between gross margin and EBITDA margin is the operating expense base (SG&A, marketing, R&D) that is expensed even though much of it builds customer and brand capital, so firms with a large gap have depressed current EBITDA relative to their economic earnings and high operating leverage, and trade at higher EV/EBITDA. Matching 3-digit industry peers on both margins at once (rather than gross margin alone) equalizes this expensed-investment share and the scope for margin expansion, while growth and net leverage match duration and financial risk.

name: sales_operating_leverage_box
mechanism: EV/Sales capitalizes not only today's cash margin but the margin the firm can reach as it scales, and that potential depends on cost structure: a firm with a high gross margin but a modest EBITDA margin carries a large fixed, expensed operating base that will be leveraged as sales grow. Hard bands on both gross margin and EBITDA margin put peers at the same current cash margin and the same operating leverage regardless of SIC code, and ranking on growth, asset turnover and size then matches how fast that leverage is realized, the capital behind each sales dollar, and the risk premium.

name: sales_value_creation_regime
mechanism: Growth raises value only when the return on new capital exceeds the cost of capital; for a firm with ROIC below WACC faster growth destroys value, so the sign and size of the growth effect on EV/Sales flips across ROIC regimes. Hard bands on EBITDA margin and on ROIC place peers in the same cash-margin and value-creation regime first, so that ranking on sales growth compares growth that is worth the same per dollar, with size added for the risk premium.

name: sales_leverage_distress_box
mechanism: Enterprise value adds debt at roughly book value, but for highly levered firms equity behaves like an option and expected distress costs reduce the true value of the operating assets, so at the same cash margin high-leverage firms show a systematically different EV/Sales than unlevered ones. A hard debt-to-assets band next to the EBITDA-margin band keeps peers in the same capital-structure and distress regime, and ranking on growth, gross margin and size matches duration, pricing power and the size premium.
